title: Finite projective cohomology over an arbitrary affine Noetherian base
statement: For affine T with Noetherian Gamma(T,O), finite coordinate type N, a closed embedding j:Y -> P(N;T) [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], and quasi-coherent finitely presented module F [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], every H^q(Y,F) [pqf-def-cohomology] is finite over Gamma(T,O), with scalars restricted along (j followed by the projective projection).

proof.text: For P=P(N;T) use its standard affine cover, separatedness over the affine base, and the Cech-to-H comparison. Model its intersections by finite infima in the opens-site Cech complex. The comparison with the alternating Cech complex identifies degree-r cochains with a product indexed by strictly increasing Fin(r+1)->N. For r >= Nat.card N no such injection exists, including when N is empty. The degree-r term and its homology vanish; transport the zero homology through the encoding and Cech-to-H isomorphisms.

For an exact segment V -> L -> Q over a Noetherian ring with V and Q finite, restrict the last map to its image. That image is finite as a submodule of Q. The restricted map is surjective and has the same kernel; Module.Finite.of_exact proves L finite.

Descend simultaneously for every quasi-coherent finitely presented G on P from degree Nat.card N. In each degree r apply the finite-source segment with the identity embedding of P. Its coherent K is finite in degree r+1 by induction, and the exact-segment argument proves G finite in degree r. Degrees above Nat.card N were covered by the vanishing bound. Finally apply the finite-source segment to j:Y->P and F in degree q; the already established projective-space assertion supplies finiteness of K in degree q+1.

proof_origin.note: P2 formalized the affine standard-cover degree bound, simultaneous descending induction, and Noetherian image/extension argument. Only the finite-source exact segment is split off; general proper coherence is not used.

theorem finite_H_projective_affine_independent
    {Y T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T] [IsNoetherianRing Γ(T, ⊤)]
    (N : Type u) [Finite N] (j : Y ⟶ ℙ(N; T)) [IsClosedImmersion j]
    (F : Y.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFinitePresentation] (q : ℕ) :
    letI : Module Γ(T, ⊤) (F.H q) :=
      Module.compHom _ (j ≫ (ℙ(N; T) ↘ T)).appTop.hom
    Module.Finite Γ(T, ⊤) (F.H q)
